items.prompt: A support assistant must summarize a ticket, use the supplied policy to draft a reply, and hand it to a specialist. If policy evidence is missing, the handoff must identify that state instead of proposing a policy answer. Which prompt design best supports this workflow?
constraints: Ticket text and policy passages have different authority.
The specialist sends the final reply.
The receiving application needs a machine-checkable handoff state.

options.text: Define the role and sequence, separate ticket and policy content, and require a structured draft-or-escalate result tied to the available evidence.
Provide several polished reply examples and let the assistant select the closest example, returning a prose note when a policy match looks uncertain.
Merge policy and ticket into one chronological conversation, then require valid JSON containing a summary and a mandatory completed reply.
Ask a second model to review the draft for helpfulness and use agreement between the two models as the signal that policy support is sufficient.

feedback.Reason: The prompt needs both an authority structure and an explicit output state for missing evidence. A fluent reply, a valid shape, or model agreement does not establish policy support.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends clear, explicit instructions and descriptive XML tags to separate instructions, context, examples, and inputs.
Details.scenarioApplication: Separate instructions, policy, and ticket data; specify the workflow; require either an evidence-grounded draft or a structured escalation with the missing requirement.
Details.errorCorrection: Examples and review can complement the design, but do not replace source authority or a machine-readable abstention path.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If all required evidence were guaranteed upstream, the prompt could have a simpler output contract; the stated missing-policy case requires an explicit alternate state.
Details.transfer: Represent known failure states in the prompt and output contract instead of requiring a complete answer for every input.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Closest-example matching can transfer a reply across different policies, and a free-form uncertainty note does not provide the required handoff state.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Chronology obscures authority, while a mandatory reply pressures the model to complete an answer even when the policy is absent.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Two helpful-looking answers can share unsupported policy assumptions; agreement is not evidence that the supplied policy supports the reply.

items.prompt: A procurement prompt sometimes follows a supplier message that says to ignore the purchasing policy. The application currently concatenates the policy and supplier text without identifying their roles. Which prompt repair addresses this failure?
constraints: The supplier message is untrusted content to be analyzed.
The purchasing policy is the authoritative instruction source.

options.text: Repeat the purchasing policy at the end of the concatenated prompt so its recency resolves conflicts with supplier text.
Increase the number of compliant supplier examples and keep the concatenated input layout to preserve compatibility with existing templates.
Have a second model rate the supplier’s request for reasonableness, and accept requests that both models consider commercially appropriate.
Separate instructions, policy, and supplier content into labeled sections and state that supplier text cannot override the governing policy.

feedback.Reason: The failure is an authority-boundary problem. Clear separation and precedence tell the model which content governs the task and which content is merely input.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says XML tags help Claude parse complex prompts unambiguously when instructions, context, examples, and variables are mixed.
Details.scenarioApplication: Use descriptive delimiters for policy and supplier text, define precedence explicitly, and evaluate adversarial supplier messages against that prompt structure.
Details.errorCorrection: Recency, examples, and agreement can affect behavior but do not establish the missing distinction between trusted instructions and untrusted content.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Prompt boundaries are guidance, not a substitute for service-side controls on consequential actions. This repair targets instruction interpretation.
Details.transfer: Make source authority explicit when a prompt includes documents that may themselves contain instructions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Recency is not an explicit authority rule and can change as the conversation or template grows.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Compliant examples do not make the untrusted text structurally distinct or resolve a supplier’s conflicting instruction.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Commercial reasonableness is a different criterion from compliance with the authoritative purchasing policy.

items.prompt: A credit assistant calls an issuance service that currently accepts amounts above an account’s limit without approval. A carefully written system prompt normally keeps proposals below the limit. What change is necessary before relying on this workflow?
constraints: Issuing a credit changes external state.
The account limit must hold even when the model proposes an incorrect amount.
High-impact credits require an authorized confirmation.

options.text: Add examples around the maximum permitted amount and evaluate more boundary cases before retaining the current service contract.
Enforce account authorization and limits in the service, require the specified approval, and retain prompt instructions as supporting guidance.
Require a second model to approve the proposed amount before passing it to the issuance service, with both models receiving the account policy.
Have a reviewer approve the assistant’s plan at session start, then allow subsequent credits under that plan to use the existing issuance endpoint.

feedback.Reason: A non-negotiable action limit must be enforced where the action executes. Prompt behavior or model agreement cannot make an accepting service reject an unauthorized credit.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic's tool guide states that the application writes the schema and executes custom tool calls, so the application remains the enforcement boundary.
Details.scenarioApplication: Validate the caller, account, amount, and required approval at the backend before issuance. The prompt can explain and follow the policy, but cannot be its only enforcement point.
Details.errorCorrection: Examples, model review, and broad session approval do not bind every concrete credit to the required service-side authorization and limit.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Prompt improvements remain useful for reducing rejected proposals. They complement rather than replace deterministic action enforcement.
Details.transfer: Put hard constraints on external effects at the execution boundary, not solely in the model’s instructions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A better benchmark can show fewer bad proposals but cannot guarantee that the accepting endpoint enforces the limit.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Both models can agree on an invalid proposal, and the backend would still execute it under the current contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A plan-level approval does not validate every subsequent account and amount or enforce the required high-impact confirmation.

items.prompt: A logistics assistant uses the same workflow across regions, with regional shipment data supplied at request time. Missing shipment fields must be visible to the operator rather than filled from likely patterns. Select TWO prompt-contract choices that support reuse and correctness.
constraints: The role, workflow, and output structure are shared.
Regional variables are validated before insertion.
The receiving workflow can request clarification.

options.text: Maintain separate complete prompt copies for every region and reconcile their shared instructions during periodic release reviews.
Fill missing values from the nearest complete shipment example, then label the entire result as an estimate for the operator.
Keep the shared role, workflow, and output rules in a reusable template with explicit validated regional variables.
Return every required field as a string so missing values and completed values fit one schema without a separate state.
Define a structured missing-data result that identifies absent fields and routes clarification instead of inventing them.

feedback.Reason: Reusable governing instructions avoid drift, while an explicit missing-data state preserves the difference between observed shipment facts and absent information.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends explicit instructions, desired output formats, and constraints so Claude does not have to infer the team's workflow.
Details.scenarioApplication: Render one common template with validated regional data and require the structured output to identify any fields that block completion.
Details.errorCorrection: Prompt copies can drift, estimated fields can be mistaken for shipment facts, and a permissive string schema does not identify why a value is absent.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A region with a genuinely different workflow may need a distinct template; changing data alone does not justify duplicating the shared contract.
Details.transfer: Separate stable behavioral rules from request variables, and encode missing information as a state the receiving workflow can act on.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Periodic reconciliation does not prevent shared rules from diverging between copies and gives up the stated common-template advantage.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: An estimate label does not satisfy the requirement to expose missing fields rather than supply invented shipment values.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A uniform type can be convenient, but without explicit missingness the receiver cannot distinguish an absent value from an ordinary string.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.c: The common template preserves one version of the shared instructions while allowing validated regional variation.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: The structured missing-data path preserves factual integrity and gives the operator an actionable clarification request.

items.prompt: A pricing assistant receives two approved templates: one says to round to whole units and the other says to preserve cents. Both are current, but overlapping requests produce inconsistent results. Which prompt-contract change should follow agreement between the policy owners?
constraints: The two sources are trusted; this is not an untrusted-content attack.
No existing precedence rule defines which instruction controls the overlap.

options.text: Encode the agreed conditional precedence in labeled template sections and use an explicit clarification state for unmatched conflicts.
Place the finance template last, keep both versions unchanged, and use stable ordering as the conflict-resolution mechanism.
Provide examples for each template separately and choose whichever template the model judges semantically closer to the request.
Run one generation per template and select the price closest to the previous accepted transaction for the same customer.

feedback.Reason: Two trusted instructions can still conflict. The prompt must express the owners’ governing rule rather than leave authority to ordering, similarity, or historical output.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic advises being clear and direct about instructions, desired output, and constraints; encoding canonical precedence and conditional rules here is the scenario's prompt-contract application.
Details.scenarioApplication: Document the agreed condition for each rounding rule, render it explicitly with the two sources, and require clarification when a request does not fit that condition.
Details.errorCorrection: Stable order and examples can influence a choice but do not establish the authorized precedence; an old transaction may belong to another rule.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the templates governed disjoint fields with no overlap, clear separation could be sufficient without a conflict rule.
Details.transfer: Resolve conflicting trusted requirements with an explicit owner-approved rule before asking a model to apply them.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Prompt position is not the agreed policy condition and can silently make one template dominate every request.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Semantic similarity does not establish which trusted authority controls a request that matches both templates.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A prior accepted price is not proof of the current request’s governing rounding rule.

items.prompt: A customer-email template renames {due_date} to {payment_due_date}. After deployment, some generated emails contain the old literal placeholder. The surrounding instructions are unchanged. Which repair targets the observed failure?
constraints: The template catalog is versioned.
Representative records can be used in render and output checks.
The failure begins with the variable-contract change.

options.text: Normalize unresolved placeholders in a postprocessor and keep the deployed template, monitoring how often the repair is applied.
Lower generation variability and retry emails containing braces, accepting the first output whose format check passes.
Add more completed email examples using the new variable and leave the old variable schema in place until the next catalog release.
Align the template, variable schema, and examples in one version, run representative render checks, and reject or roll back a failing release.

feedback.Reason: The regression aligns with a template-variable contract change. Repairing and testing that contract is more direct than treating unresolved placeholders as generation variance.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends establishing clear success criteria and empirical tests before improving a prompt; versioning and render checks here are scenario-authored controls for the changed template contract.
Details.scenarioApplication: Update all references consistently, render representative records, test for unresolved variables, and release only a version that satisfies the contract.
Details.errorCorrection: Postprocessing, retries, and additional examples can mask symptoms while the mismatched input variable remains unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If render checks showed correct variables and the error originated in untrusted content, authority or input handling would become the relevant diagnosis instead.
Details.transfer: Treat changes to prompt variables as versioned interface changes with executable render checks.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A postprocessor may not know the intended missing value or field mapping; it does not repair the broken render contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Generation variability is not the demonstrated cause, and a brace-free result could still contain an invented due date.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: New examples cannot reliably compensate for an old schema that still binds the wrong variable name.

items.prompt: A claims assistant returns schema-valid JSON with decision="approve" and limit=5000, citing approved policy P17. The cited P17 passage requires manager approval but contains no 5,000 limit; that amount appears only in stale P12 evidence. What should happen before the result is sent to the analyst?
constraints: A field-to-source-span check is available.
A specialist can review an escalation.
The schema and citation allowlist checks have already passed.

options.text: Pass the result because its types and source ID are valid, and ask the analyst to verify the numeric value during ordinary review.
Check material fields against current evidence, mark the unsupported limit unknown, and abstain or escalate; retain separate action-authorization checks.
Replace the citation with P12 so the number has a matching span, while retaining P17 as the governing policy for the approval decision.
Ask the same model to confirm its confidence in the limit and pass results above the application’s confidence threshold.

feedback.Reason: Structural validity and an approved citation ID do not establish that the cited current policy supports the claim. The unsupported amount and approval cannot be passed as a grounded policy result.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends structuring long document context and asking Claude to ground responses in relevant document passages; the field-to-span gate and escalation are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Compare the amount and decision with their current supporting spans, expose the unsupported field, and route the case for clarification or review rather than publishing a confident approval.
Details.errorCorrection: Analyst review, a stale supporting citation, and self-confidence do not repair the mismatch between the current governing evidence and the generated claim.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If each field came from a validated typed policy record through deterministic mapping, that mapping could establish support without a separate model entailment check.
Details.transfer: Validate what structured fields mean and what supports them, not just whether they parse or contain an approved source identifier.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The proposed handoff still presents an unsupported value as a completed result despite the known evidence mismatch.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A stale passage can explain where the number came from but cannot authorize it under the current policy.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: The model’s confidence is not evidence that P17 contains or permits the stated limit.

items.prompt:
A claims assistant returns {decision: approve, limit: 5000} in the required JSON schema and cites policy revision P17. The current P17 passage explicitly supports a 5,000 limit, records the required manager approval, and the account scope is valid; a stale P12 passage is also present but is not the governing revision.

How should the assistant handle the apparently conflicting evidence?
constraints: P17 is the current governing revision and explicitly supports the 5,000 limit.
Manager approval A88, account scope, and field-level evidence spans are valid.
P12 is stale and must not override the current policy record; final credit execution remains separately authorized.

options.text: Pause the handoff, treat P12 and P17 as coequal sources, and ask an owner to choose the applicable limit before proceeding.
Ground every field in current P17 and approval A88, hand off for review, and leave execution behind service authorization.
Return the JSON fields without policy and approval citations because schema validity is sufficient for analyst review.
Apply the older P12 limit conservatively and escalate the claim even though P17 and A88 support the requested result.

feedback.Reason: The evidence state changes from unsupported stale text to complete current support; grounding requires delivery with references, not abstention simply because an older conflicting passage exists.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends structuring long document context and asking Claude to ground responses in relevant document passages; the field-to-span gate and escalation are scenario controls. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The current governing evidence and approval record support every material field, so the assistant should produce a grounded ready-for-analyst result while retaining separate execution authorization.
Details.scenarioApplication: Parse the schema, verify the decision and limit against the current P17 span and approval A88, include those references in the analyst handoff, mark the result grounded and ready for analyst review, and leave any final credit execution behind the service authorization gate.
Details.errorCorrection: The older P12 passage is not the governing revision, while current P17 and A88 support the result; abstention would discard valid evidence without resolving the actual authority order.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If P17 omitted the limit or A88 were missing or the account scope invalid, return to the sibling decision: mark the unsupported field unknown and abstain or escalate.
Details.transfer: Use measured slice quality, service limits, and authority boundaries together; choose the least complex route that clears every stated floor and revisit it when the evidence changes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The scenario identifies P17 as governing and A88 as valid; treating the stale passage as coequal creates an unnecessary block instead of grounding the handoff in current evidence.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A valid shape does not prove the material decision or limit; the handoff must bind fields to the current P17 span and A88.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Choosing stale policy over the current governing revision creates an unnecessary escalation and fails to use the valid current evidence.

items.prompt:
Prompt version 7 adds a conditional refusal rule and a risk_reason field to a claims assistant. On a 10,000-case replay, JSON validity falls from 99.6% to 96.8%, correct refusals rise from 93% to 97%, p95 is unchanged, and the production floor is 99% valid output.

Which change should be made before any production canary?
constraints: Prompt version 7 raises correct refusals to 97% but lowers JSON validity to 96.8%.
The production validity floor is 99%, and every invalid record is traceable to a field-level parser error.
The template can be revised, replayed, canaried, and rolled back with refusal behavior retained.

options.text: Ship version 7 because correct refusals improved, then let downstream parsers handle the 3.2% invalid records.
Revert immediately to version 6 and remove the refusal rule so the prior validity score is preserved.
Retain the refusal rule, repair the conditional schema, replay, and canary only a version meeting 99% validity while retaining the measured refusal improvement.
Keep version 7 unchanged and add a parser retry after each invalid response, using the retry result as the new contract.

feedback.Reason: The conflicting safety and contract metrics require a versioned prompt decision plus field-level observability rather than choosing one aggregate metric.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends establishing clear success criteria and empirical tests before improving a prompt; versioning and render checks here are scenario-authored controls for the changed template contract. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The safer refusal behavior is valuable, but the prompt contract cannot ship below the output validity floor; revise the contract and guardrail together with observable outcomes.
Details.scenarioApplication: Keep the refusal requirement, revise the schema/template examples so risk_reason is emitted only under the documented condition, replay the cases, and canary only a version that clears 99% validity while retaining the refusal gain.
Details.errorCorrection: Invalid records breach the production contract and make downstream handling unsafe; unchanged latency does not make malformed decisions acceptable.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If revised version 8 reaches 99.2% validity with at least 96% correct refusals, canary it; if not, keep version 6 and escalate the unresolved safety requirement.
Details.transfer: Use measured slice quality, service limits, and authority boundaries together; choose the least complex route that clears every stated floor and revisit it when the evidence changes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Invalid records breach the production contract and make downstream handling unsafe; unchanged latency does not make malformed decisions acceptable.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: That protects validity by discarding the measured safety improvement; the contract should be repaired and tested instead of choosing between the two goals.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A retry layer does not repair the conditional schema that causes invalid output and can hide a versioned contract defect while remaining below the 99% floor.
